title: Repairs stall between diagnosis and parts arrival

retrieve_on.symptom_narrative: Technicians identify a part, office staff ask suppliers, and customers approve quotes. The gaps between those steps last days. An approval sent to a technician never reached purchasing. Shelves and spreadsheets disagree, and warranty return dates get missed.
retrieve_on.workflow_context: Nine-person business PC and laptop repair provider.

discriminating_questions.question: What is waiting right now?
discriminating_questions.synthetic_answer: The sheet says waiting for parts, but a supplier is actually waiting for a submodel.
discriminating_questions.diagnostic_value: Status must expose the next dependency.
discriminating_questions.branch_if_answer_differs: A confirmed manufacturer backorder will not be shortened by reminders; communicate alternatives and expected dates instead.

discriminating_questions.question: Where does approval arrive?
discriminating_questions.synthetic_answer: Email and direct messages, sometimes only to the technician.
discriminating_questions.diagnostic_value: Capture approval in the repair record.
discriminating_questions.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

discriminating_questions.question: Who checks overdue items?
discriminating_questions.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

discriminating_questions.question: Are return and loaner obligations tracked?
discriminating_questions.synthetic_answer: They are handwritten on paper labels.
discriminating_questions.diagnostic_value: Repair closure is not the only completion condition.
discriminating_questions.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

positive_mechanism: Handoffs lack an accountable next action, complete part identity and explicit deadlines.
counterexample: A confirmed manufacturer backorder will not be shortened by reminders; communicate alternatives and expected dates instead.
minimum_evidence: A simulated approval message predates purchase by four days.
A simulated supplier request lacks the full part number.
A simulated return label has an approaching deadline.
process_intervention: Assign one repair owner; require exact part verification before purchase; separate waiting for information, approval, supplier and customer.
automation_candidate: Track dependency states, deadline reminders and linked loan/return obligations; prepare customer updates from verified status.
unknowns: Supplier return policies and alternative-parts approval rules remain unverified.
stop_rule: If discriminating evidence is absent or conflicting, return an unresolved hypothesis plus a targeted question, not a confident solution.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Purchasing, loaner and warranty lifecycle extensions are required.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.
